headline: New stores lift sales; tariff refund flatters profit growth
summary_short: Floor & Decor's fiscal Q2 net sales rose 3.0% y/y to $1.25B despite a 2.1% comp-store-sales decline, as diluted EPS jumped to $0.89 from $0.58 a year ago — though $45.2M of that gain came from a one-time IEEPA tariff refund; adjusted diluted EPS was flat at $0.58.
summary_long: Net sales rose 3.0% y/y to $1.25B (+8.5% q/q) as five new warehouse stores offset a 2.1% comp-sales decline; comps improved from -5.1% in April to nearly flat in June. GAAP operating income (+51.4% y/y) and diluted EPS ($0.89 vs $0.58) were both lifted by a one-time $45.2M IEEPA tariff refund; adjusted diluted EPS was flat at $0.58 and adjusted EBITDA rose just 1.2% to $152.0M. Cash grew to $320.6M on stronger operating cash flow; the company refinanced its term loan and ABL facilities in June, extending maturities to 2033/2031. FY2026 outlook: sales $4.77-4.99B, diluted EPS $2.20-2.45, adjusted EBITDA $550-585M.

drivers.explanation: Comp-store sales improved through the quarter, from a 5.1% decline in April to nearly flat in June, which management attributed to the resilience of the business model and disciplined execution.
Five new warehouse store openings (ending the quarter at 281 stores) offset a 2.1% comparable-store-sales decline, lifting net sales despite uneven demand for larger discretionary flooring projects.

GAAP gross margin expansion (+430bp) was driven almost entirely by a one-time $56.2M IEEPA tariff refund recognized in cost of sales; adjusted gross margin, which excludes the refund, actually fell 20bp y/y.
Most of the y/y operating-income growth reflects the same one-time tariff refund flowing through cost of sales rather than underlying demand improvement.
Net income and diluted EPS both benefited from the $45.2M tariff refund and a smaller $1.3M debt-extinguishment loss; adjusted net income was roughly flat y/y at $63.0M.
GAAP diluted EPS rose to $0.89 from $0.58 almost entirely on the tariff refund; adjusted diluted EPS, which excludes it, was flat at $0.58.
Cash increased on higher operating cash flow (H1 $278.4M vs $155.3M), driven by a $108.6M rise in trade payables partially offset by a $112.7M increase in receivables.
The term loan balance was little changed after the company refinanced its term loan and ABL facilities in June 2026, extending maturities to 2033 and 2031 at similar principal amounts.
